section_summary: This section centers on a 1948 dispute over the yen’s exchange rate. General MacArthur urged an immediate increase in the military conversion rate, while State and Treasury officials pressed for a general commercial rate and sent a technical mission to Japan. The section also contains correspondence about a former prisoner of war’s yen, charitable remittances to China, and converting Japanese property proceeds into dollars.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Far Eastern Commission authority over exchange policy
subfiles.about: Discusses whether an exchange rate directive must be submitted to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: The author argues that an interim Far Eastern Commission directive could establish the policy basis for a yen commercial rate, allowing detailed implementation through SANACC without prolonged Commission delay. Clearance should follow discussion with Draper’s group.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about charitable remittances to China
subfiles.to: Department of State, Foreign Transfer Division
subfiles.about: Asks whether missionary funds can be sent through the American consul in Chungking and paid in U.S. currency.
subfiles.summary: Battista seeks a means of remitting clients’ funds for charitable work in China.

subfiles.title: Reply on remittances to China
subfiles.about: Explains lawful banking channels and Chinese exchange rules for incoming remittances.
subfiles.summary: Consuls cannot handle ordinary exchange transactions; banks can remit funds, but Chinese rules prohibit payments in U.S. currency.

subfiles.title: File note requesting earlier Sherry correspondence
subfiles.about: Requests earlier papers for the Dean Sherry case.
subfiles.summary: Fraleigh asks records staff to locate the prior correspondence.

subfiles.title: Indexing note for Judge Sherry letter
subfiles.about: Requests indexing and return of Judge Sherry’s letter.
subfiles.summary: Fraleigh asks that the letter be indexed and returned with earlier papers.

subfiles.title: Handwritten routing note on Sherry correspondence
subfiles.about: Routes earlier Sherry correspondence to Fraleigh.
subfiles.summary: The note appears to identify earlier letters supplied for the case.

subfiles.title: Judge Sherry’s account of Japanese prisoner of war pay
subfiles.about: Seeks redemption of yen paid by Japanese captors at its value when his pay accrued.
subfiles.summary: Sherry itemizes monthly balances credited to him as a prisoner of war, reaching 4,079 yen at liberation. He argues that Japan should redeem the yen at the earlier exchange value rather than its depreciated value when paid.

subfiles.title: Reply to Judge Sherry concerning war claims
subfiles.about: Responds to Sherry’s inquiry about payments received during captivity.
subfiles.summary: Maglich acknowledges Sherry’s letter and encloses the War Claims Act of 1948.

subfiles.title: State position on MacArthur’s exchange rate proposal
subfiles.about: Reports an interdepartmental discussion of MacArthur’s proposal to raise the military yen rate.
subfiles.summary: Army representatives favored an immediate rise to 225 yen per dollar. State and Treasury representatives preferred sending a mission to assess an early commercial rate, then considering a military rate change if needed.

subfiles.title: MacArthur telegram proposing a 225-yen military rate
subfiles.to: William H. Draper Jr., Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Requests an urgent increase in the military conversion rate from 50 to 225 yen per dollar.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur argues that the 50-yen rate harms occupation personnel, missionaries, businesses, airlines, tourists, and remittance recipients while encouraging black market transactions. He derives a proposed 225-yen rate from comparative consumer price indexes and says it would not affect foreign trade. He recommends retaining 50 yen per dollar in the Ryukyu Islands.

subfiles.title: Cover memorandum on yen exchange rate papers
subfiles.about: Forwards proposed State policy and a second SCAP telegram before talks with Draper.
subfiles.summary: Fearey highlights Treasury’s objection to changing the military rate without a commercial rate.

subfiles.title: Hilliard memorandum on an exchange rate for the yen, draft copy
subfiles.about: Argues for State leadership and an early commercial yen rate.
subfiles.summary: Hilliard favors a commercial rate over MacArthur’s proposed military rate change. He suggests a rate around 250 yen per dollar, subject to technical study and National Advisory Council review.

subfiles.title: Hilliard memorandum on an exchange rate for the yen, clean copy
subfiles.about: Presents the same argument for prompt establishment of a commercial yen rate.
subfiles.summary: Hilliard says changes to a military rate offer only temporary relief and may undermine confidence in the yen. He urges a commercial rate by July 1 and suggests about 250 yen per dollar, pending expert review.

subfiles.title: Reasons against an interim military rate change, draft copy
subfiles.about: Lists reasons to establish a commercial rate before changing the military rate.
subfiles.summary: Hilliard warns that another military rate could damage confidence in the yen and urges a small technical mission.

subfiles.title: Briefing for Lovett on the yen exchange rate
subfiles.about: Summarizes the exchange rate dispute and the mission sent to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman describes MacArthur’s request for a 225-yen military rate and State and Treasury’s preference for a general commercial rate. A mission led by Ralph A. Young had departed on May 15; the departments aimed to settle policy by July 1.

subfiles.title: Reasons against an interim military rate change, clean copy
subfiles.about: Repeats Hilliard’s case for a commercial rate and a small mission.
subfiles.summary: Hilliard says a commercial rate addresses underlying problems and avoids further uncertainty and black market pressure.

subfiles.title: Personnel for proposed mission to Japan
subfiles.about: Recommends government personnel for the exchange rate mission.
subfiles.summary: Havlik favors McDiarmid and Strong as State representatives and suggests several potential mission leaders.

subfiles.title: Tentative list of exchange rate mission leaders
subfiles.about: Lists prospective leaders from banking and the Federal Reserve.
subfiles.summary: Candidates include Williams, Riefler, Sproul, Young, Szymczak, Hardy, and Burgess.

subfiles.title: Treasury letter opposing MacArthur’s exchange rate proposal
subfiles.about: Urges a general exchange rate instead of broadening the military conversion rate.
subfiles.summary: Treasury argues that multiple conversion rates would distort trade and delay a durable general rate. It describes Japanese inflation as manageable enough for action and supports a small technical group to consult with MacArthur’s staff.

subfiles.title: Draft SANACC minutes on yen exchange rate agreement
subfiles.about: Records an agreement to study a general rate and set a July 1 decision point.
subfiles.summary: State, Treasury, and Army agreed to send a technical mission to Japan. If no position on a commercial rate emerged by July 1, Army could change the military rate after consulting State and Treasury.

subfiles.title: Draft appointment and terms of reference for Ralph A. Young
subfiles.about: Appoints Young to lead the yen exchange rate mission and sets its instructions.
subfiles.summary: The draft names mission members and directs them to consult SCAP on a commercial rate or, if premature, an interim military and financial conversion rate. It requests a report by June 16.

subfiles.title: Mission personnel and SANACC minutes
subfiles.about: Forwards personnel advice and proposed SANACC minutes.
subfiles.summary: Hilliard relays background on Young and other possible mission leaders.

subfiles.title: Saltzman letter transmitting proposed cable to SCAP
subfiles.about: Sends an agreed State and Treasury draft response to MacArthur’s June 29 cable.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman requests priority Army review of the proposed joint cable.

subfiles.title: Draft joint cable to SCAP on a single general exchange rate
subfiles.from: Departments of State, Treasury, and Army
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Directs establishment of a general yen rate with a strengthened stabilization program.
subfiles.summary: The draft rejects MacArthur’s objections to an early single rate, arguing that delay risks worsening inflation and wasting U.S. rehabilitation aid. It calls for Japanese government responsibility under SCAP direction, an October 1 target, stronger tax and credit controls, wage stabilization, budget restraint, and improved materials allocation. Limited subsidies could ease the transition to world prices.

subfiles.title: Report on decision to send exchange rate mission
subfiles.about: Reports the decision to send a yen exchange rate mission to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Fearey lists expected members and unresolved choices for mission leadership.

subfiles.title: SANACC agreement on yen rates, duplicate copy
subfiles.about: Duplicates the agreement to send a technical mission and consider an interim rate if needed.
subfiles.summary: The agreement sets July 1 as the decision point for a commercial rate.

subfiles.title: Telegram announcing departure of the exchange rate mission
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Advises SCAP that a seven-person technical mission will depart for Tokyo on May 15.
subfiles.summary: Marshall asks for assistance to the mission and identifies McDiarmid as its State member.

subfiles.title: SCAP telegram on foreign exchange controls
subfiles.to: Department of the Army; Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Explains SCAP controls on foreign exchange and payments by foreign agencies in Japan.
subfiles.summary: SCAP says foreign exchange must be reserved for essential imports. Foreign agencies pay some charges in foreign currency; for direct local transactions, agencies without yen income must obtain yen through authorized conversion at the military rate.

subfiles.title: Referral of Serge Lekomtzeff case
subfiles.about: Requests advice on converting proceeds from Lekomtzeff’s Japanese property into U.S. money.
subfiles.summary: The division asks for a paragraph to include in its reply to Salamato.

subfiles.title: Passport Agency forwarding letter
subfiles.about: Forwards a communication received about Lekomtzeff.
subfiles.summary: The agency submits the enclosed letter for Shipley’s attention.

subfiles.title: Salamato inquiry about financing Lekomtzeff’s immigration
subfiles.about: Asks how Lekomtzeff can lawfully obtain dollars from selling property in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Salamato explains that Lekomtzeff needs U.S. money for transport and immigration and owns real estate in Japan that he hopes to sell.

subfiles.title: Reply to Salamato on converting Japanese property proceeds
subfiles.about: Explains the lack of a means to convert Japanese property sale proceeds into dollars.
subfiles.summary: Doherty says Japan lacks available dollars for such conversion and advises that Salamato may provide funds if Lekomtzeff is admitted to the United States.

subfiles.title: Report on the exchange rate mission and MacArthur’s response
subfiles.about: Summarizes the Young mission’s proposed rate and MacArthur’s objections.
subfiles.summary: The mission recommends a single controlled rate of 270–330 yen per dollar by October 1, supported by tax, budget, credit, wage, and materials measures. MacArthur argues that imposing those reforms so quickly could collapse Japan’s economy and seeks an immediate military rate increase instead. The memorandum continues beyond page 302.
